intro.title: Build typed command history undo redo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed command history system that supports undo and redo operations. You will learn how to manage state changes in a type-safe way using TypeScript. The core concept involves implementing a command pattern with arrays to track history and a pointer for navigation. You'll use TypeScript interfaces, generics, and array methods to ensure your commands are strongly typed and reversible. By the end, you'll have a reusable module that can track, undo, and redo user actions safely.
intro.usecase: The command pattern with undo/redo functionality is essential in professional applications where users need to reverse or replay actions. You'll find this in design tools like Figma or Photoshop where every brush stroke or layer adjustment can be undone, in code editors like VS Code that track file changes, and in form-heavy applications like CRM systems where sales representatives might need to revert accidental data entries. As a developer, implementing typed command history ensures users can confidently interact with your application knowing they can recover from mistakes while you maintain type safety across all operations.
